# FIPS crypto module audit of serving-stack images

## Description

Produce a complete, validated inventory of cryptographic module usage across every image in the model serving stack — the KServe component images and the Platform Operator serving data plane images — identifying each image that links non-validated crypto libraries, whether the usage sits in the request path, and the remediation approach each finding requires. The strategy states that non-validated crypto is linked "in several images" but does not say which images or which libraries; resolving that is technical work whose answer determines the scope and approach of all downstream remediation. The resulting module inventory is also a required input to the FIPS compliance evidence package.

## Scope

- Enumerate all serving-stack images in scope: KServe component images (serverless and raw deployment modes) and Platform Operator serving data plane images.
- For each image, inventory the linked cryptographic libraries/modules and classify each as validated or non-validated for FIPS 140-3 purposes.
- Classify each non-validated usage as request-path or non-request-path.
- Produce a per-image remediation recommendation (library replacement, build-time crypto mode enablement, code change) with effort class.
- Characterize current baseline behavior of the stack on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster (what fails today and how).
- Deliverable: audited module inventory plus remediation plan, in a form reusable as the module-inventory section of the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every serving-stack image in scope has a completed inventory entry listing its linked cryptographic libraries with a validated/non-validated classification.
- Every non-validated finding is classified as request-path or not, and carries a remediation recommendation — no unassigned findings.
- Findings are reproducible: re-running the inventory method on a sampled image yields the same classification.
- The remediation plan covers 100% of non-validated findings and each recommendation names the images it applies to.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): establishes which images violate the validated-crypto requirement and what fixing each takes — the factual basis for the remediation work.
- HLR-2 (P0): produces the module inventory required in the compliance evidence package.

# Remediate KServe images to validated cryptographic modules

## Description

Modify and rebuild the KServe component images so that the serving request path uses only validated cryptographic modules and the images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters. The specific changes (library replacements, build-time crypto mode enablement, or code changes) are determined by the outcome of the FIPS crypto module audit of the serving stack.

## Scope

- Apply the remediation plan produced by the crypto module audit to every KServe image it flags: replace or rebuild against validated crypto modules, removing non-validated crypto from the request path.
- Carry changes in the KServe midstream repositories so images can be rebuilt and attested in the serving-stack build pipeline.
- Verify remediated images serve inference requests correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters (both serverless and raw deployment modes where applicable).
- Preserve existing behavior on non-FIPS clusters.
- Fold in any caption, screenshot, or reference touch-ups that fall out of these changes; substantive new documentation is handled separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An image scan of every remediated KServe image shows no non-validated crypto library linked in the request path, measured against the audited inventory.
- Remediated images serve inference requests successfully on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
- Remediated images continue to serve inference requests on non-FIPS clusters — no functional regression.
- Remediated images build green in the serving-stack build pipeline, and the resulting build attestations are retained for the compliance evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): KServe portion — all KServe serving-stack images run on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds

## Description

Add a gating CI check to the serving-stack build pipelines that fails any build which reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, so FIPS compliance is enforced continuously rather than re-audited manually. The set of disallowed crypto usages the check enforces is defined by the FIPS crypto module audit's validated inventory.

## Scope

- Implement a regression detection check that inspects serving-stack build outputs for non-validated crypto usage, keyed to the audited inventory of disallowed libraries and usages.
- Wire the check as a gating (build-blocking) step in the serving-stack build pipelines, covering both the KServe component images and the Platform Operator serving data plane images.
- Produce actionable failure output identifying the offending image and library.
- Include a self-test fixture (a known-bad and a known-good build input) so the check's behavior is verifiable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A serving-stack build that reintroduces a known non-validated crypto usage from the audited inventory fails the gating check.
- A clean serving-stack build passes the check.
- The check is gating on every serving-stack build pipeline in scope — a failing check blocks the build.
- The currently remediated image set passes with no false positives.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# FIPS compliance evidence package assembly and submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and drive it through security review board sign-off at the defined milestones to submission at the external accredited certification lab. This epic spans the whole serving stack (KServe component images and Platform Operator serving data plane images).

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory from the FIPS crypto module audit of the serving stack.
- Collect build attestations from serving-stack builds that passed the FIPS regression gate, and FIPS-enabled-cluster test results for every remediated serving-stack image.
- Package the evidence to the certification lab's stated requirements.
- Obtain security review board sign-off at the defined submission milestone.
- Submit the package to the external accredited certification lab and record the lab's triage confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, build attestations from serving-stack builds that passed the FIPS regression gate, and FIPS-enabled-cluster test results for every remediated serving-stack image.
- The evidence package passes security review board sign-off at the defined submission milestone.
- The evidence package is submitted to the external certification lab, and the lab's triage confirmation is recorded.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months. Lab scheduling and review-board cadence are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort — this is a schedule risk on this epic, not a condition its deliverable can produce. The acceptance criteria are written at the engineering completion point (package assembled, sign-off obtained, submitted and triaged).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab.
